scope: Unique final profile reports for one compiled PWA build. Chromium and Firefox passed all ten checks. Windows WebKit UI/catalogue revalidated after correcting a runner race with the asynchronous library refresh; its five native-media cases remain blocked by the documented Windows WebKit 26.5 transport limitation.

checks.name: setup.open: compiled PWA and real service worker
driving.empty: idle playback, empty queue and all viewport sizes
driving.wake-preference: toggle persists and close releases acquired native locks
driving.setup: favorites, playlist and download are created through UI
checks.dataSource: Product UI and controlled provider HTTP

checks.name: driving.library: selected collection persists through tabs and rotation
driving.transport: play, pause, next, previous and selected queue use one audio

longTitleLayout.scope: CSS-only two-line h1 text stress; media metadata, queue and product state are unchanged

checks.name: driving.exit: exit button, Escape and browser Back preserve uninterrupted audio
checks.browserBackSource: Real browser history API; phone system Back and car hardware unverified

checks.name: driving.media-session: registered system handlers operate the car-mode player
checks.source: Native registration observed; handlers invoked by QA. Actual Bluetooth buttons/car display unverified.

checks.name: driving.podcast: skip 30/15 seconds uses same episode and fits all viewports
checks.title: Episodio QA Uno

checks.name: driving.offline: downloaded collection starts without provider response bytes
checks.title: Canción QA Uno

profiles.networkTransport: Puppeteer HTTP interception and Playwright UI; production modules and SW retained.

No external upstream. Self-signed fixture certificate accepted only in this disposable QA context.
